comparator.name: Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated 2026–2027 guide controls this generic Dutch full-time Law LLB. The curriculum introduced from 2023 is fully present across three sixty-credit years. Four compulsory Amsterdam Law Firm modules each carry zero credits; they remain required and are not added to the 180-EC total. The fifteen-credit Year-3 elective space remains open. Insolvency is retained from the original public-list ordering; the dated menu lists Labour Law first but permits either and provides no default. This is a restricted course choice, not a formal route. Law and Practice uses the permitted mediation/negotiation simulation rather than inventing an internship host. The thesis requires 120 EC already registered in SIS three weeks before semester start; completing both earlier years meets this condition before the selected Spring thesis. No fixed future cohort timetable is guaranteed beyond the dated curriculum.

components.name: Grondslagen van het recht
components.note: The Dutch-taught Law LLB includes compulsory Amsterdam Law Firm 1.1 and 1.2 alongside Year-1 subjects. They carry zero additional credits and develop legal research, writing, oral advocacy and mediation.

components.name: Verbintenissenrecht
components.note: Amsterdam Law Firm 2.1 is a compulsory zero-credit legal-research and writing module alongside Year 2. The research plan must receive at least 5 before the research report may be written.

components.name: Materieel strafrecht
components.note: Amsterdam Law Firm 2.2 is a compulsory zero-credit moot-court module. Its criminal-law or administrative-law variant is taken alongside, or after, the relevant substantive and procedural courses. This pathway completes both sets in Year 2.

components.name: Recht en Praktijk
components.note: This example chooses the permitted mediation and negotiation simulation. Students act as mediators in a legal case, practising listening, perspective-taking and negotiation. No internship host or placement is assumed.

components.name: Vrije keuzeruimte
components.note: Fifteen credits remain genuinely open for electives, a minor or study abroad. No particular course package, host or minor is imposed.

components.name: Insolventierecht
components.note: Insolvency Law is the retained permitted integration choice, combining earlier private-law subjects, company law and questions of distribution and justice. Labour Law is an alternative, not an additional component.

components.name: Fundamentele rechten
components.note: Fundamental Rights integrates earlier constitutional, European and international law with legal philosophy and applications across legal fields.

components.name: Bachelorscriptie FdR
components.note: Entry requires at least 120 degree credits already recorded in SIS three weeks before the semester begins; expected but unregistered results do not count. Both earlier years are completed before the Spring thesis. The thesis includes an individual legal paper and oral presentation and defence before two assessors; no fiscal specialisation or particular topic is assumed.

It implements the explicit academic basis “Legal research, writing, case analysis, procedure and practical dispute work” and “Sustainability and environmental legal questions”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Foundations of European Union Law examines EU institutions, competences, legal effect, remedies, citizenship and free movement through current judgments and legal cases. It implements the explicit academic basis “International, European and fundamental-rights law”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest interdisciplinary law-and-society programme owns the broad direct interests. Two distinct feasible directions deepen the public/international/European and private/commercial sides of the curriculum. Together these reach the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine AI, institutional change, governance and regulation. UCR studies business/economic and social implications; UvA develops legal analysis of digitalisation, platforms and government algorithms.

Both examine contractual obligations, risk allocation, performance and remedies through legal cases. UCR concentrates on transnational commercial transactions; UvA develops Dutch contract and liability doctrine.

Both develop negotiation, conflicting perspectives and structured dispute-resolution practice. UCR uses bargaining simulations; the chosen UvA pathway uses mediation and negotiation around a legal case with explicit reflection on professional roles.
Both develop the nature of law, legal sources, interpretation and case analysis within a social and normative framework.
Both examine fundamental-rights law, protection institutions and philosophical justifications. UvA integrates the operation of rights across Dutch and international legal fields.
Both examine criminal acts, causation, intent, guilt, offences, justifications, excuses and participation as substantive grounds and limits of criminal liability.
Both develop public international law through legal sources, institutions, state responsibility, force and contemporary legal cases. The relationship is substantive but partial.

Both examine state organisation, rights, government powers and constitutional constraints. UCR compares systems and includes administrative principles; UvA establishes Dutch constitutional and administrative law.
Both develop contract, tort and property concepts through legal problems. UCR compares legal systems; UvA establishes Dutch private-law foundations including their social context.
Both examine the EU legal order, institutions, national effects, citizenship, free movement and remedies.
Both develop reasoned ethical positions on conflicting obligations. UCR provides general ethical theory and practical argument; UvA applies professional codes and role-specific dilemmas for lawyers.

Both examine normative foundations of rights, authority and the liberal political/legal order. UvA additionally develops specific jurisprudential theories, legal positivism, natural law and legal interpretation.
Both substantively examine constitutional democracy, institutions, representation and threats to democratic order. UCR uses empirical comparison; UvA develops a legal constitutional-redesign project.
